thread:
maya (AE): Heads-up — MercuryTrade (enterprise trading platform) is asking for a binding Q3 commit. Profile: 520 rps sustained during 75m market window, avg 19k tokens/session with bursts to 1.2k concurrent sessions. They want predictable p50 < 280ms and a market-hours SLA (13:30-14:45 ET). They asked for a concrete reserved GPU + burst credit plan and an ops handoff (prewarm, failover, KMS).

ben (Sales Eng): 520 rps @19k tokens is heavy but doable with quantization + aggressive KV caching. Do they accept int8/int4 variants? Also confirm Private vs Dedicated.

maya (AE): They want Private VPC and HSM/KMS. Legal also flagged EU data residency for a subset of traffic. Procurement wants monthly baseline + burst-credit SKU + a worst-case overage example. CFO wants amortized $/token.

kiran (Solutions): Immediate comments: (1) KV-shard affinity matters — large contexts create >1GB KV per session unless we prefix-truncate. Recommend per-tenant prefix namespaces with selective prefix warm to reduce KV state. (2) Quantized model reduces GPU-hours ~2.4x conservative.

olga (SRE): Quick thumb: with prefix-KV and per-request batching, effective tokens/sec per A100-equivalent GPU increases a lot; real numbers come from perf runs. Interim conservative rec: reserve 7 GPUs (quantized) for baseline, allow 3 burst GPUs that can be prewarmed on schedule.

diego (Infra): Private deploy note: AZ spread for SLA will require capacity reservations across 2 AZs; burst capacity cannot rely on our shared pool. Lead time for AZ placement + HSM cert exchange ~3 weeks. Also, HSM integration must be validated before prewarm jobs run.

ben (Sales Eng): Procurement wants a simple table: baseline reserved GPUs, burst credits bucket (minutes or token bucket), prewarm run cost, and worst-case scenario if spikes 4x/month. Can we model burst credits in minutes (e.g., 1200 burst-minutes/month) for them?

kiran (Solutions): Yes. We'll express burst as both token credits and burst-minutes to make it intuitive. Example conservative pricing line: reserved 7 GPUs (quantized) monthly + 3 burst GPUs with 1200 burst-minutes/month (equivalent to X token credits). Provide FP16 alternative (reserve 18 GPUs baseline).

olga (SRE): Ops runbook excerpt for handoff (can paste into RFC):
```
# autoscale / prewarm excerpt
autoscale_policy:
  baseline_replicas: 7
  max_burst_replicas: 3
  burst_window_sec: 1200   # 20min per burst slot
  burst_minutes_bucket_monthly: 1200
  kv_cache:
    enabled: true
    shard_affinity: per-tenant
    persistence: true
    ttl_hours: 18
  prewarm_jobs:
    - cron: "15 12 * * 1-5"   # 75m window -> prewarm 75m before
      replicas: 9
  degrade_policy:
    queue_depth_threshold: 220
    sustained_sec: 60
    fallback_model: "mercury-7b-quant"
```
Notes: (a) prewarm should do a dry-run with KMS decrypt check and fail fast if HSM permissions invalid, (b) KV warm is incremental: first 10-15m most valuable.

diego (Infra): Add infra gating step: prewarm job must run KMS smoke test (decrypt sample) and post KMS status to ops channel; if smoke fails, prewarm should abort and page SRE. Also include EU-residency routing rules in the deployment manifest.

ben (Sales Eng): CFO wants amortized $/token. kiran — can you draft two lines (quantized vs fp16) using a conservative 2.4x factor and include warmup billing note?

kiran (Solutions): I'll do that. Warmup billing note: synthetic warm requests are billed as normal inference; we minimize cost by warming high-frequency prefixes only and by limiting warm-run length. We'll show a separate warm-run cost estimate.

olga (SRE): One more ops detail: configure a soft-fallback that routes low-risk queries to cached-response layer when queue depth > 150 for >30s. Hard degrade to smaller model only after sustained >60s at >220 queue depth. That balances quality and tail latency.

maya (AE): Action items: (1) olga to run perf bench on their model/container for 8k and 19k contexts — need artifacts by EOD today or we'll use conservative sizing; (2) kiran to draft price table (quantized vs fp16) + amortized $/token and warmup cost; (3) diego to list Private infra lead times, HSM checklist, and EU routing notes; (4) ben to prepare procurement-facing one-pager with worst-case overage scenarios.

security-bot: Security checklist reminder — outstanding: HSM integration proof, KMS decrypt smoke test, SOC2 evidence, vendor encryption attestation. All required before Private deploy sign-off.

ben (Sales Eng): One enterprise blocker flagged by their legal  they insist on SLA >99.95 for market window. If so, we must recommend active-active across AZs and add +1 baseline GPU per AZ as failover capacity. I'll note that in the CFO sheet.

diego (Infra): Confirmed — AZ active-active raises baseline GPU reservations and impacts burst-minute availability. I'll quantify delta in lead-time doc.

okga (SRE): typo: *olga. Also, I'll include a sample canary rollout: route 5% to new revision, monitor p50/p99 and queue, then ramp over 10min with KV-warm checkpoints.

maya (AE): Great. I'll update MercuryTrade and ask for the perf artifacts right away. Re-open after olga posts bench results. Thanks team :thumbsup:

ben (Sales Eng): I'll attach a short CFO-friendly spreadsheet once kiran posts numbers.

kiran (Solutions): Drafting now — will post by EOD PST.

security-bot: Noted. Please attach SOC2 report and HSM attestation to the vendor packet.

maya (AE): Closing thread until perf & pricing posted.
